Android from the foundation · Puzzle 15 of 15

Frames, jank and ANRs

Drawing the screen is just another message in the main thread's queue. So one slow message doesn't only delay a tap: it stops the screen from being drawn.

The problem

In puzzle 14, the main thread ran messages one at a time. Now suppose one message takes a long time, like reading a big file, or a Thread.sleep(6000) in onCreate()Your override of this method is what the main thread calls when system_server says "create". 1864 protected void onCreate(@Nullable Bundle savedInstanceState) {Activity.java, line 1864 · AOSP frameworks/base ↗, which pauses the thread for 6 seconds. What does the user see?

See it

Save this diagram as a GIF

The building block

The screen is redrawn about 60 times a second. Each redraw is a frame, and each one must be ready within about 16 milliseconds (1000 ms ÷ 60). Drawing a frame is a message in the main thread's queue too.

If a message takes longer than that, the frames behind it come late, and the app visibly stutters: jank.

If a touch waits in the queue for 5 seconds, system_server notices and shows the "App isn't responding" dialog: an ANR. That's why slow work (files, network, big calculations) belongs on another thread, never on the main thread.

The analogy

The clerk also has to repaint the shop window 60 times a second. One long phone call, and the window freezes; keep a customer waiting long enough, and the town hall puts up a sign: "not responding".

Right. One message at a time: the touch waits behind the sleep, and after 5 seconds comes the ANR.

Not quite. Nothing is stopped: system_server shows a dialog and the user decides.

A message takes 100 ms, and there are no touches. Is that an ANR?

Right. 100 ms ÷ 16 ms ≈ 6 frames late: jank. A touch waiting 5 s means an ANR.

Not quite. An ANR is about a touch waiting 5 seconds. 100 ms is jank: late frames.

Why should file reading go on another thread?

Not quite. It can; it just mustn't, because frames and touches wait behind it.

Right. Keep every main-thread message short.

What you now know

A frame is due about every 16 ms. A message that takes longer makes frames late: jank. A touch that waits 5 seconds gets the "App isn't responding" dialog: an ANR.
